metric.definition: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

reading.body:
Power purchase agreements are how data center operators secure the generation they need to operate, and the mix of sources they choose—nuclear, renewable, or gas—now shapes both AI infrastructure feasibility and energy transition outcomes.

PPAs lock in price and supply for years or decades. They allow operators to commit to new facilities before construction, which matters because data centers take time to build and power grids take longer still. A PPA is how an operator de-risks a project. It is also how the industry finances new generation, since developers can build renewable or nuclear plants on the strength of a signed contract rather than speculation about future demand.

Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular reactor commitments, became the defining PPA story of the AI era. This matters because nuclear provides dense, continuous power with minimal land use and no carbon emissions, solving three constraints at once. But PPAs say nothing about what actually gets built, how fast it comes online, or whether contracted capacity ever reaches promised output. They are financial instruments, not facts on the ground.
